title: Sections-tensor comparison commutes with shifts
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and finite extensions $E\subseteq L$ of $\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subseteq\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Apply exact sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ termwise, with the canonical constant-value maps $\mathcal O_F\to\Gamma(s,R_F)$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Let
$$
 \theta_K:\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)
$$
be the canonical sections-tensor comparison specified in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], where tensor on the left is ordinary tensor of module complexes and on the right is ordinary derived change of sheaf rings. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, $\theta_{K[m]}=\theta_K[m]$ under the standard termwise shift identifications for sections and scalar tensor; these identifications are compatible with zero and successive shifts.

Explicitly, on a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the representing map in degree $r$ is
$$
 \Gamma(s,P^r)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,P^r\otimes_{R_E}R_L),\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto\text{the sheaf tensor section }a\otimes b_s,
$$
where $b_s\in R_L(s)$ is the constant section defined by $b$ and the sheaf tensor is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These maps form a natural map of complexes, commute with the standard integer shifts, and induce the displayed equality in $D(\mathcal O_L)$ independently of the chosen resolution.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor presheaf and its sheafification. Integer-shift compatibility and descent for the particular sections-tensor comparison are the extracted agent argument for the final display of blueprint def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, not a separate assertion of Tag 03EK.
